record.title: Preprint reports forced-choice answer formats suppress refusal mechanisms in hazardous-knowledge evaluations
record.summary: An arXiv preprint published on 2026-11-05 compares multiple-choice and open-ended versions of WMDP questions on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. The authors report that models often answer forced-choice hazardous-knowledge questions even when they refuse matched open-ended questions, and present tuned-lens, refusal-direction and attention-head interventions as a mechanistic account. The causal head-ablation result is robust on Llama-3.1-8B but not Qwen3-8B. These are author-reported preprint results; no independent replication was inspected.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors posted arXiv:2611.08639v1 on 2026-11-05, reporting an analysis of multiple-choice versus open-ended WMDP prompts on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that forced-choice prompts are almost never refused even on items often refused in open-ended form, with similar MCQ correctness across open-ended refusal groups. They report a mid-layer answer-letter commitment, lower alignment with a refusal direction, and format-dependent suppression across biosecurity, chemistry and cybersecurity items.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that ablating selected answer-letter attention heads partially restores refusal on Llama-3.1-8B while layer-matched random-head controls do not; the corresponding causal result did not hold robustly on Qwen3-8B.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: This single preprint does not establish that the measured mechanism generalizes across model families, current frontier systems or safety-evaluation formats beyond the tested models and WMDP prompts; independent reproduction was not inspected.

evidence_gaps.description: The WMDP format and mechanism findings are author-reported results from two instruction-tuned models; no independent matched reproduction was inspected.
The study does not test current frontier models or establish whether the measured activation mechanism transfers to other architectures and evaluation settings.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported mechanism generalizes, forced-choice hazardous-knowledge scores may not measure refusal activation, changing safety-benchmark design and interpretation. Evidence is an unreplicated preprint covering two instruction-tuned models, with the stronger causal result limited to Llama-3.1-8B.
limitations: The central empirical results are author-reported in one preprint and have not been independently reproduced in this activation.
Open-ended prompts rewrite option-dependent stems for 394/1,273 biosecurity, 176/408 chemistry and 260/1,987 cybersecurity items, so format and wording are not perfectly isolated.
The causal head-ablation result is robust on Llama-3.1-8B; Qwen3-8B evidence is weaker and the refused-item samples are small.
The paper studies two instruction-tuned models and the WMDP dataset; it does not establish current frontier-model or cross-benchmark generalization.
brief.summary: An arXiv preprint published on 2026-11-05 compares multiple-choice and open-ended versions of WMDP questions on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. The authors report that models often answer forced-choice hazardous-knowledge questions even when they refuse matched open-ended questions, and present tuned-lens, refusal-direction and attention-head interventions as a mechanistic account. The causal head-ablation result is robust on Llama-3.1-8B but not Qwen3-8B. These are author-reported preprint results; no independent replication was inspected.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report lower refusal in forced-choice WMDP prompts than matched open-ended forms and provide tuned-lens, refusal-direction and attention-head intervention analyses.
technical.demonstrated_result: Publication of the v1 preprint is established. The reported experimental outcomes remain CLAIMED and unreplicated.
technical.implementation_status: Preprint and appendices are available; linked code was not executed.
technical.mechanism: The authors hypothesize that answer-format instructions drive mid-layer answer-letter commitment that competes with refusal formation; head ablation supports the causal account for Llama-3.1-8B but not robustly for Qwen3-8B.
technical.regime: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B on WMDP biosecurity, chemistry and cybersecurity questions; author-run preprint experiments.
technical.reproducibility: arXiv HTML and appendices were inspected; no independent reproduction or execution of the linked code was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched open-ended questions and layer-matched random-head ablations; the wording rewrite affects a stated subset of prompts.

brief.title: Preprint reports forced-choice answer formats suppress refusal mechanisms in hazardous-knowledge evaluations
brief.why_it_matters: If it generalizes, a safety score from multiple-choice hazardous-knowledge questions can reflect knowledge retrieval without measuring whether a model activates refusal in open-ended use. This could change how such evaluations are designed and interpreted; two models, rewritten prompt variants and author-run analyses do not establish a general effect.
